description: Write a Python ETL script (requests + pandas) for fintech_app that incrementally syncs invoices from an API using updated_since. The script should: (1) read the last watermark (2025-03-01T10:05:00Z in the sample), (2) request invoices with updated_since = watermark minus a 5-minute overlap to tolerate clock skew and in-flight transactions, (3) for each invoice id keep the record with the greatest updated_at from the response, (4) upsert into the target on id, never replacing a target row with an older record, (5) parse amount strings such as '1,200.50' into Decimal, (6) set the new watermark to the maximum updated_at seen. In the sample, rows are tagged with _dataset = target or api_response.
edge_cases: The overlap re-delivers inv1 as of 10:00, which already exists; an append-only load would duplicate it
inv1 appears twice in the response; only the 10:07 'paid' version survives
'1,200.50' contains a thousands separator and must become 1200.50, not 1.2 or NaN
New watermark is 2025-03-01T10:08:00Z (max updated_at seen), not the request time
An empty response leaves the watermark unchanged
common_failure_modes: FM2: No overlap window, so records committed late with earlier updated_at values are missed forever
FM1: Append instead of upsert duplicates re-delivered records
FM4: Thousands separators break numeric parsing
